title: Responses compatibility shim: contract tests, behavioral gaps, and canary rollout plan
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Define and implement a lightweight compatibility shim and automated contract test suite that maps Redwood Responses-compatible API semantics to OpenAI Responses semantics. Focus areas: streaming event parity, function/tool call lifecycle, structured-output integrity (JSON schema enforcement), and error/fallback mappings for hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
updates: 2025-02-10 - Ticket created by Jordan Lee with initial scoping and proposal to prototype a shim that operates at the API gateway layer.

2025-02-14 - Spike completed: documented differential catalog for OpenAI Responses events vs Redwood streaming events (see links). Identified 4 high-risk behavioral gaps: partial chunking semantics, tool call nesting, structured output normalization, and event ordering under retries.

2025-02-20 - Prototype shim v0 implemented (gateway-level translator) and exercised with internal mock of OpenAI Responses. Early findings: streaming token-level 'delta' vs 'message' envelope mismatch requires buffering or token-reconstruction for Redwood client parity.

2025-02-25 - Design review with Runtime and API teams. Decided to prioritize a 'best-effort streaming parity' option with opt-in strict mode for structured outputs where we validate and re-emit canonical events.

2025-03-01 - QA added contract tests for function/tool call sequences. Found race conditions when tool calls return before 'tool_call.completed' event is emitted by provider; added idempotency token requirement in shim translation.
2025-03-04 - Canarization plan drafted: run shim for 5% of hosted traffic in region us-west-2 with telemetry for latency, fidelity loss, and tool-call error rates.
implementation_notes: Shim lives in API gateway; minimal runtime CPU overhead target <2ms median per request.
Streaming handler will reconstruct partial tokens into Ruby/JS-friendly 'message' events when requested by client compatibility flag.
Introduce 'compat_mode' query header (values: off|best-effort|strict) to control behavior per-call and per-customer.
Function/tool calls: persist per-request call state in a small in-memory store with fallback to Redis for long-running calls in Dedicated/Private.

Structured output enforcement: integrate JSON schema validator during streaming 'end' and emit structured_error event when validation fails. In strict mode, return 422 with structured validation details.
Error mapping: translate provider-specific transient errors to Redwood canonical error codes; add automatic retry/backoff for idempotent function calls.
Observability: instrument stream event counts, reorder events, validation failures, and extra-latency introduced by shim.
acceptance_criteria: Automated contract test suite passes against mock OpenAI Responses for 95% of cataloged scenarios.
Canary in us-west-2 shows <=5% p99 latency regression compared to baseline for covered routes at 95% load profile.
Tool/function calling flows maintain idempotency and consistent lifecycle events in >99% of synthetic runs.
Structured output strict mode rejects invalid payloads with clear error details and a migration guidance link.
risks: Buffering streaming tokens to reconstruct messages may increase tail latency and memory pressure for long-lived streams.
Private deployments with air-gapped constraints may not be able to fetch provider error schemas; need local fallback mapping.
Observed semantic mismatches could lead to user-facing behavioral regressions for edge cases requiring manual customer migration steps.
Rollout complexity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private increases support overhead during canary.
notes: Design feedback from Priya Raman: add migration guide for customers relying on partial-token streaming.
Action item: coordinate with Console team for UI toggle for compat_mode and per-customer telemetry flags (owner: Sarah Patel).
Follow-up spike proposed to quantify memory impact under sustained 1000 concurrent streams.
